newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends firmer after dollar supply rises.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends firmer after dollar supply rises.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 665-675 per dollar in light interbank volume, up from 720-750 in the morning and 695-698 at the previous close, due to a rise in dollar supply in the afternoon, dealers said.
"High dollar levels in the morning and low lev liquidity of banks and clients encouraged dollar supply while demand was low also due to the lev shortage," one dealer said.

Traders partly attributed the low lev liquidity to last week's Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) decision to cut commercial banks' minimum required reserves that banks can use for emergency refinancing each month to 30 percent from 40 percent.
This was the second cut in as many weeks aimed at curbing banks' liquidity before large interest and maturity payments on government securities due in January.
"After some clients bought the dollars they needed in the morning, foreign currency demand shrank in the afternoon," another dealer said.
The BNB was not seen selling or buying dollars today, dealers said. BNB officials were not available for comment. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
